screening.reason: Reports a resting-state fALFF + structural-MRI fusion analysis of ABIDE II (discovery) and ABIDE I (replication) comparing ASD subtypes to typically developing controls and predicting ADOS/SRS scores; satisfies inclusion 1-4.

evidence_spans.text: DSM-IV-TR diagnosed Asperger’s disorder (n = 79), pervasive developmental disorder-not otherwise specified [PDD-NOS] (n = 58) and Autistic disorder (n = 92) from ABIDE II were used as discovery cohort, and ABIDE I (n = 400) was used for replication.
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE II ASD subtype groups (Asperger's n=79, PDD-NOS n=58, Autistic n=92) used as discovery cohort, ABIDE I (n=400) as replication.

evidence_spans.text: Subjects with ASD (n = 229) and the corresponding TDCs (n = 126) were selected from the ABIDE II [29, 30], which is hosted by the 1000 Functional Connectome Project/International Neuroimaging Data-sharing Ini- tiative (INDI) from multiple international sites (9 sites, Additional file 1: Table S1).
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE II discovery sample: 229 ASD, 126 TDC from 9 sites.

evidence_spans.text: we removed outlier datasets with mean FD exceeding 1 mm, as well as head motion exceeding 2.0 mm of maximal translation (in any direction of x, y or z) or 1.0° of maximal rotation through- out the course of scanning.
evidence_spans.claim: Motion QC excluded scans with mean FD>1mm or motion >2.0mm/1.0 degree.

evidence_spans.text: to calculate fALFF [34], the sum of the spectral amplitude values in the 0.01–0.08 Hz low-frequency power range was divided by the sum of the amplitudes over the entire detectable power spectrum (range: 0–0.25 Hz).
evidence_spans.claim: fALFF computed as ratio of low-frequency (0.01-0.08Hz) spectral power to total power (0-0.25Hz).

evidence_spans.text: the preprocessed multimodal MRI features were jointly analyzed by a fusion-with-reference model called “MCCAR + jICA”
evidence_spans.claim: Fusion of fALFF and GM voxel maps used MCCAR+jICA, guided by ADOS scores.

evidence_spans.text: Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and superior/middle temporal cortex are the primary common functional– structural covarying cortical brain areas shared among Asperger’s, PDD-NOS and Autistic subgroups.
evidence_spans.claim: DLPFC and superior/middle temporal cortex are common functional-structural covarying areas across ASD subtypes.

evidence_spans.text: negative fALFF in anterior cingulate cortex unique to PDD-NOS subtype; and negative thalamus–amygdala–caudate fALFF unique to the Autistic subtype.
evidence_spans.claim: Subtype-unique negative fALFF patterns: ACC for PDD-NOS, thalamus-amygdala-caudate for Autistic subtype (putamen-parahippocampus for Asperger's).

evidence_spans.text: The identified subtype-specific patterns are only predictive for ASD symptoms manifested in the corresponding subtypes, but not the other subtypes.
evidence_spans.claim: Subtype-specific brain patterns predict only the corresponding subtype's symptoms, not other subtypes.

evidence_spans.text: models can be generalized to predict ADOS and SRS scores for the corresponding subgroup from ABIDE I, but not for the other groups
evidence_spans.claim: Prediction models trained on ABIDE II generalized to predict ADOS/SRS in ABIDE I for the matching subgroup only.

evidence_spans.text: site-out analysis (details can be found in Additional file 1: “Reproducibility” section) in the ADOS-guided fALFF and GMV fusion on the whole ASD group to check whether the site effect will contribute to current ASD pattern.
evidence_spans.claim: Leave-one-site-out analysis showed ASD covarying pattern consistent across sites.

assessments.support: Subjects with ASD (n = 229) and the corresponding TDCs (n = 126) were selected from the ABIDE II [29, 30], which is hosted by the 1000 Functional Connectome Project/International Neuroimaging Data-sharing Ini- tiative (INDI) from multiple international sites (9 sites, Additional file 1: Table S1). Selection criteria also required age <35 and males only.
Table 1 reports demographic/clinical info by subtype and TDC; ABIDE II (9 sites) discovery, ABIDE I (17 sites) replication.

risk_of_bias.summary: Detailed ABIDE II discovery / ABIDE I replication design with explicit motion QC thresholds, site/age/IQ deconfounding, leave-one-site-out and cross-cohort checks; feature is voxel-wise fALFF rather than an atlas-based connectivity measure.

charting.title: Common and unique multimodal covarying patterns in autism spectrum disorder subtypes
charting.primary_goal: Identify common and subtype-unique functional (fALFF) and structural (GM) covarying brain patterns among Asperger's, PDD-NOS and Autistic subgroups, and test their ability to predict ADOS/SRS symptom scores in an independent cohort.
charting.study_setting: Multi-site (9 sites ABIDE II discovery; 17 sites ABIDE I replication)
charting.diagnosis_assessment: most of the sites used the ADOS and Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) scores to diagnose ASD
charting.medications_therapies: Medication use of participants reported in Table 1
charting.severity_levels: ADOS and SRS total/subdomain scores used as severity measures
charting.dataset_openly_available: The supervised fusion code has been released and integrated in the Fusion ICA Toolbox (FIT), which can be downloaded and used directly by users worldwide. The multimodal MRI data used in this study can be accessed upon application from ABIDE consortium.
charting.dataset_available_request: ABIDE data accessible upon application from the ABIDE consortium
charting.feature_types: Voxel-wise fALFF (functional) and GM volume (structural) maps
charting.specific_features: fALFF and GM voxel maps fused via MCCAR+jICA guided by ADOS scores; no atlas/parcellation (voxel-wise analysis)
charting.importance_method: Back-reconstruction of group differences and correlation of components with ADOS subdomains
charting.top_features_identified: DLPFC and superior/middle temporal cortex common across subtypes; subcortical regions unique per subtype (putamen-parahippocampus Asperger's, ACC PDD-NOS, thalamus-amygdala-caudate Autistic)
charting.feature_change_direction: negative fALFF in anterior cingulate cortex unique to PDD-NOS subtype; and negative thalamus–amygdala–caudate fALFF unique to the Autistic subtype.
charting.specific_algorithms: MCCAR+jICA fusion (discovery) + multiple linear regression (cross-cohort symptom-score prediction)
charting.validation_methodology: Discovery in ABIDE II, cross-cohort replication/prediction in independent ABIDE I sample; leave-one-site-out sensitivity analysis
charting.performance_metrics: Correlation between predicted and true symptom scores; normalized root mean squared prediction error (NRMSE)
charting.key_performance_results: models can be generalized to predict ADOS and SRS scores for the corresponding subgroup from ABIDE I, but not for the other groups
charting.summary_key_findings: DLPFC and superior/middle temporal cortex are shared functional-structural covarying areas across ASD subtypes; each subtype shows unique subcortical fALFF alterations correlated with distinct ADOS subdomains, and subtype-specific brain patterns predict symptom severity only within the matching subtype when generalized from ABIDE II to ABIDE I.
charting.features_associated_disorder: negative fALFF in anterior cingulate cortex unique to PDD-NOS subtype; and negative thalamus–amygdala–caudate fALFF unique to the Autistic subtype.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Both associational (subtype vs TDC) and predictive (ADOS/SRS regression); ABIDE II discovery (229 ASD: 79 Asperger's/58 PDD-NOS/92 Autistic, 126 TDC, 9 sites) and ABIDE I replication (n=400, 17 sites)
narrative_row.methods: SPM12 preprocessing, voxel-wise fALFF (functional) and GM volume (structural) maps, ADOS-guided MCCAR+jICA multimodal fusion, back-reconstruction for group differences, multiple linear regression cross-cohort prediction of ADOS/SRS, leave-one-site-out sensitivity analysis.
narrative_row.outcomes: DLPFC and superior/middle temporal cortex are shared covarying regions across subtypes; each ASD subtype shows a unique subcortical fALFF alteration pattern linked to distinct ADOS subdomains; subtype-specific patterns predict symptoms only within the matching subtype when generalised from ABIDE II to ABIDE I.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Male-only sample, not generalisable to females or the general ASD population; voxel-wise fALFF rather than atlas-based connectivity; feature definition and prediction both drew on ABIDE II data before independent ABIDE I testing.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Demonstrates a discovery/replication design spanning ABIDE II and ABIDE I with explicit QC thresholds and code release (FIT toolbox), useful for cohort reconstructibility assessment; illustrates subtype-stratified (rather than binary ASD/TDC) analysis.
